newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss plan to sell gold over 10 years for fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss plan to sell gold over 10 years for fund.

text.p: Switzerland's plan to use official gold reserves to create a humanitarian fund for victims of the Holocaust and other recipients would entail selling gold over a 10-year period, Swiss National Bank Chairman Hans Meyer said.
But he told a news conference such sales -- worth "several billion" Swiss francs -- would not have to disrupt the gold market and had no implications for the stability of the Swiss franc.

He said the planned foundation would be financed with a substantial proportion of valuation gains achieved on SNB gold reserves, now valued at around 12 billion francs at the fixed legal parity of 4,595 francs per kg.

"On the basis of a more realistic -- albeit still cautious -- valuation, several billion francs could be transferred in gold to the foundation," he said, permitting investments yielding several hundred million francs a year annually.
The foundation would invest the capital at its disposal and use the income to achieve its objectives, he added.

"It is envisioned that the foundation would sell the gold transferred to it in the market over a period of approximately 10 years and invest the proceeds in interest-bearing assets," Meyer said. "In view of the modest annual volume of such sales and given a prudent approach, which is in the foundation's own interest, this should be possible without market disruption," he added.

"The transfer of a part of the National Bank's gold reserves to a foundation has no implications for the stability of the Swiss franc," he said, adding that banknotes would continue to have 100 percent gold coverage if the gold was valued at the market price.
He said it would take around two years to lay the legislative foundation for the move.
